name: Uranus from Voyager 2, January 24, 1986
blurb: A planet that spins tipped on its side, about 51,100 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 2's wide-angle camera through orange, green and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: A close view of part of Uranus, fully lit, from about 960,000 kilometers from Uranus's center, 17 hours before Voyager 2's closest approach to Uranus on January 24, 1986. Voyager 2's visit in January 1986 is still the only one any spacecraft has made to Uranus.

claims.text: about 51,100 kilometers across at the equator (JPL: equatorial radius 25559 km)
rotates at a nearly 90-degree angle from the plane of its orbit
